title: New Bus Lanes in Riverside: Who Wins and Who Loses?
instructions: 这是为B1–B2成人学习者设计的原创模拟阅读材料（非官方雅思，也不对应任何官方分数）。先通读文章，再完成10道题。题目全部为英文，解释为中文。注意：本材料重点复习被动语态、顺序连接词，并新学“定语从句与分词短语的辨认”。请先看语法讲解，再做题。
passage:
A. Riverside is a mid-sized city with a busy river, three bridges, and a lot of old roads. Last year, the city council introduced a new transport policy. Two main roads in the city centre were changed. One lane on each road was closed to private cars and opened only to buses and bicycles. The plan was called 'Clean Lanes'. The council said the plan was designed to reduce traffic and air pollution. Many people supported the idea, but not everyone was happy.

B. The new rules were introduced in March. First, the council held three public meetings. Then, engineers studied traffic on the two roads for six weeks. After that, the changes were tested for two months. Finally, the policy was made permanent in September. During the test, bus travel times fell by about 15 percent. Air quality near the roads also improved. However, drivers who used the roads every day were angry. They said the new lanes made their journeys longer. Some shop owners on Bridge Street also complained. They said fewer customers came by car, so they lost money.

C. The council listened to these complaints. In October, it published a report written by a team of transport experts. The report showed that bus passengers and cyclists benefited most. People living near the roads also benefited, because the air was cleaner. But drivers and some local businesses lost out. The report suggested two solutions. The first was to build new parking areas near the edge of the city centre. The second was to give small shops a reduction in their business taxes. The council is now discussing these ideas.

D. Not everyone agrees with the report. A group of drivers, called 'Fair Roads', says the policy is unfair. They argue that people who live outside the city and drive to work have no good bus service. They also say that the council did not ask them before making the changes. The council replies that the public meetings were open to everyone. It also says that new bus routes to the outer areas will start next year. Meanwhile, some environmental groups want the city to go further. They want more Clean Lanes and fewer cars in the centre.

E. The story of Riverside is not unusual. Many cities are trying to reduce cars in their centres. The effects of such policies are often unequal. People who take the bus or ride a bike usually gain. People who must drive often lose. The challenge for city leaders is to listen to all groups and to find fair solutions. As one council member said, 'A good transport policy must work for everyone, not just for some.'

grammar.title: 被动语态、顺序连接词、定语从句与分词短语的辨认
grammar.explanation: 本课复习被动语态（be + 过去分词，强调动作承受者）和顺序连接词（first, then, after that, finally）。新学内容是辨认定语从句和分词短语：定语从句用who/which/that等引导，放在名词后补充说明；分词短语用-ing或-ed形式放在名词后，起类似作用，但更简短。例如：a report written by experts（分词短语）相当于a report which was written by experts（定语从句）。
grammar.example: In October, it published a report written by a team of transport experts.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence in the passive voice.
options: The council introduced the policy last year.
The policy was introduced by the council last year.
The policy introduced the council last year.
The council was introduce the policy last year.
answers: The policy was introduced by the council last year.
questions.explanation: 被动语态结构为be + 过去分词，强调政策被引入。
questions.evidence: The policy was introduced by the council last year.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct order words to complete: ______, the council held three public meetings. ______, engineers studied traffic.
questions.explanation: 顺序连接词First表示首先，Then表示然后，符合逻辑顺序。
questions.evidence: First, the council held three public meetings. Then, engineers studied traffic.

questions.prompt: Which part is a defining relative clause? 'The report which was published in October showed clear results.'
questions.explanation: 定语从句由which引导，修饰report，说明哪份报告。

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a participle phrase?
options: The man driving the bus was very friendly.
answers: The man driving the bus was very friendly.
questions.explanation: driving the bus是现在分词短语，修饰the man，相当于who was driving the bus。
questions.evidence: The man driving the bus was very friendly.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive form: The new rules ______ in March.
questions.explanation: 规则是被引入的，用被动语态were introduced。
questions.evidence: The new rules were introduced in March.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a relative clause correctly?
options: The shop who lost money closed.
The shop which lost money closed.
The shop lost money which closed.
The shop closed which lost money.
answers: The shop which lost money closed.
questions.explanation: 先行词shop是物，用which引导定语从句。
questions.evidence: The shop which lost money closed.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct order words: ______, the changes were tested. ______, the policy was made permanent.
questions.explanation: After that表示在那之后，Finally表示最后，符合时间顺序。
questions.evidence: After that, the changes were tested. Finally, the policy was made permanent.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct reduced form of 'the people who live outside the city'?
options: the people live outside the city
the people living outside the city
the people lived outside the city
the people to live outside the city
answers: the people living outside the city
questions.explanation: 定语从句who live可简化为现在分词短语living outside the city。
questions.evidence: the people living outside the city
